nodes.text: FAST · ON-DEVICE AI The provided text is a summary of the United States Constitution , focusing on its establishment of a federal government with legislative, executive, and judicial branches. Its main points are: • [1] The Constitution creates a three-branch system (legislative, executive, judicial) where Congress consists of two houses: House of Representatives (based on population) and Senate (equal representation per state). Both must meet at least once a year on December 3rd unless otherwise designated by law. • [2] The legislative branch shares powers with the President regarding bills; if passed by both houses, it goes to the President who signs or returns it. Orders require presidential approval before taking effect. Section 8 grants Congress powers like taxation, borrowing money, regulating commerce, and establishing a navy. • [3] The executive is headed by an elected President for four years who serves as Commander-in-Chief and can appoint officials and grant pardons. The judicial branch includes a supreme court with specific jurisdictions over ambassadors/states and general cases, while all criminal trials must include juries. • [4] The document was adopted on September 17, 1787. It defines treason as levying war against the U.S., aiding its enemies, or providing them aid and comfort (requiring two witnesses for conviction). Article Four mandates admission of new states with Congress's consent and guarantees each state a republican form of government. Summary of all 9 pages.
